clue.text: Finding Asti in 22 is the hardest part

definitions.meaning: the four letters ASTI make up half of the eight-letter answer to 22, which names a famous battle
an idiom for the most difficult step of a task, which once done means success is close

explanation.surface: Tracking down a bottle of Italian sparkling wine in a seaside town is the toughest bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 22-across is HASTINGS, the battle of 1066; ASTI sits inside it and is four of its eight letters, so finding it is literally half of that battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says that completing a key step means most of the struggle is already over.

clue.text: Some schoolboys, rears beaten, finally get detention

parts.note: a house is a division of the pupils at a British boarding or public school

indicators.note: the word rears is knocked about into a new order
signals the last letter of the word get

explanation.surface: Pupils who had their backsides caned also end up kept in after school.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools divide pupils into houses, so a group of schoolboys is a HOUSE. 'beaten' turns REARS into ARRES, and 'finally' gives T from 'get'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confined to one's home by legal order is a form of detention.

clue.text: I can't remember drinking that!

parts.note: the words of a drinker who has forgotten everything, as happens in myth to those who drink from the underworld river of oblivion

explanation.surface: A hungover reveller denies all memory of the drink in question.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the shades drank from this underworld river and forgot their earthly lives.

clue.text: Having a measure of computing power, a fear to hear of crashes

indicators.note: says the word for fear is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: terror is extreme fear
flops are failures, things that crash

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of hearing about computer crashes has a gauge of processing power.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR said in a non-rhotic accent sounds like TERA, the prefix for a trillion; 'Having' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Teraflops counts trillions of floating-point operations per second, a standard gauge of supercomputer speed.

clue.text: Every method has better option

definitions.meaning: ... read literally is every route or manner of doing something
a bettor (one who bets) may choose to back a horse both to win and to be placed

explanation.surface: Every approach comes with an improved alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a punter, one who bets, not the comparative of good.
explanation.definitionFit: An each-way stake in horse racing is a wager split between win and place, a choice open to a punter.

clue.text: A short language course

indicators.note: the word for the language is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: Scots is the Germanic language of Lowland Scotland

explanation.surface: An abbreviated set of lessons in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like part of 'language course', but it is the definition: a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Leaf cut up, perhaps, to make this much?

indicators.note: suggests these nine letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Tea leaves chopped up might make about one cup's worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' reads like the anagram signal, but all three words Leaf cut up are the fodder and 'perhaps' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup's worth of tea is a measured amount, the quantity the clue calls this much.

clue.text: The worst place, it's commonly said, by some distance

indicators.note: a common or Cockney pronunciation drops the opening h sound

parts.note: hell is the worst place imaginable

explanation.surface: Hell is a long way off, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H as a Cockney speaker would turns HELL into the old unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old English measure of cloth length, about 45 inches.

clue.text: Bet that's not negotiable any longer

definitions.meaning: the Irish pound, no longer legal tender since the euro replaced it

explanation.surface: A wager that can no longer be bargained over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiable' means usable as money: the Irish punt was replaced by the euro in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Punt means a gamble, and it was also the Irish pound, a currency now withdrawn.

clue.text: Repaired trike should be green

parts.note: a mended tricycle can be ridden again, and an environmentally green item can be reprocessed for reuse

explanation.surface: An eco-minded instruction that a fixed tricycle ought to be environmentally friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be reprocessed into new material is green, and a repaired cycle can be cycled again.

clue.text: Medicinal plant is fine, always in small numbers

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
ever means always
few means a small number

explanation.surface: A healing herb is fine, though only ever found in small quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like herb traditionally taken for headaches and fevers, hence a medicinal plant.

clue.text: Most reliable game in trial

indicators.note: places the game inside the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: The most dependable sport to be tried out.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of true, meaning the most faithful or dependable.

clue.text: What stops one condemning a description of Miss Darling?

definitions.meaning: a redeeming quality that prevents one from condemning someone outright
Grace Darling, the lighthouse keeper's daughter who rescued shipwrecked sailors in 1838

explanation.surface: What keeps us from judging a woman known for her rescue?
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling is a British heroine who rowed out to save survivors of a wreck off Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: A redeeming feature offsets faults; Grace Darling was literally a Grace who was saving lives.

clue.text: Dispatched to glory, Ted the low-lifer

indicators.note: the words are sent off and broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A lowlife called Ted is killed and sent to glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low-lifer' is witty: a cave dweller lives low down, under the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave dweller literally lives low down, and figuratively a boorish lowlife.

clue.text: One may hang by the neck, when one's topped

definitions.text: One may hang by the neck, when one's topped

parts.words: One may hang by the neck, when one's topped
parts.note: reads like an execution, but describes a prize worn on a ribbon round the neck by whoever comes top

explanation.surface: Grim talk of hanging by the neck after being executed.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-place award at the Olympics hangs on a ribbon round the winner's neck.

clue.text: What happens to autumn trees? Head off to listen

indicators.note: the first letter of the phrase is removed

parts.note: in autumn leaves drop from trees

explanation.surface: In autumn the trees shed, and someone departs to listen in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' removes the first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening secretly to a private conversation is to eavesdrop.

clue.text: Odd number in short game

indicators.note: the name of the game loses its final letter

parts.note: fives is a handball game played in a walled court, like squash with hands

explanation.surface: An uneven tally in an abbreviated match.
explanation.walkthrough: FIVES is a British court game in which the ball is hit with a gloved hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Five is not divisible by two, so it is an odd number.

clue.text: Return vegetable to ship

indicators.note: the word for the vegetable is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: the leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: Sending a vegetable back to a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Keel names the spine of a vessel and poetically the vessel itself.

clue.text: Ill-fed man's sharp pain, eating cooked laver

indicators.note: the pain swallows the other letters inside it

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

indicators.note: the seaweed's letters are prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: A hungry man suffers a sharp pain after eating cooked seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: Laver is an edible seaweed, so 'cooked' fits the kitchen picture while signalling the anagram; 'man's' carries the definition, its 's a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A starveling is a person or animal thin and weak from lack of food.

clue.text: What's wrong — are you against?

indicators.note: the word what is wrongly arranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
art is the archaic form of are with thou

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry asking what's the matter and whether you object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are you' gives ART as in 'thou art'; 'wrong' rearranges WHAT into ATHW.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across or in opposition to, hence against.

clue.text: End of play causes puzzlement

definitions.meaning: in cricket, ... is the close of a day's play

explanation.surface: Close of play leaves everyone bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'stumps' is called when play ends for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumps marks the end of a cricket day, and it also means baffles.

clue.text: Succeeded in taking high road to peninsula

parts.note: S is short for succeeded in genealogies
taken as written
the A1 is the great main road in Britain, written as A and I

explanation.surface: A traveller manages to take the main road down to a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; here the 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the triangular peninsula in Egypt between the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba.

clue.text: Hurrying south, Harold's objective?

parts.note: hasting is an old word for hurrying
S is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: King Harold hurrying south to meet the Normans.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1066 King Harold marched south to fight William at Hastings.
explanation.definitionFit: King Harold marched to Hastings, where he fought and died, so it was his destination.

clue.text: One responsible for rain damaging drain

indicators.note: the word drain is damaged into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A flood damages a drain after heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Indra is the Hindu god of rain and thunder.

clue.text: Crowning glory as a fern?

parts.note: a young woman's hair is her crowning glory, and a delicate fern shares the name

explanation.surface: Could a fern be someone's crowning glory?
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's hair is her crowning glory, and the same name belongs to a delicate fern.

clue.text: See man in sea sail off at last

indicators.note: takes the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Spot someone out at sea as the sail finally comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' and 'in' are link words; ALF is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alf, short for Alfred, is a man's name.

clue.text: Double fight heard

indicators.note: says the word for fight is taken as spoken

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two

explanation.surface: A two-way fight is reported.
explanation.definitionFit: Dual means twofold or double.

clue.text: Make sense of season, wearing best fabric

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
in means wearing, as in dressed in
top means best
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Dressing for the season in your finest fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: When details make sense, they come together into a coherent arrangement.
